summary.headline: Digitide Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9.2% YoY to INR 800 crores, but adjusted PAT fell to INR 11 crores on wage code and accounting charges.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue reached INR 800 crores, up 2.5% QoQ and 9.2% YoY, with Tech and Digital at 31.1% of mix and international at 38.1%. EBITDA was INR 88 crores (11% margin), absorbing about INR 4 crores of one-time wage code impact. Adjusted PAT fell to INR 11 crores from INR 24 crores in Q3, mainly due to lease-accounting finance cost and a residual value policy change raising depreciation; reported PAT was INR (-5) crores after a INR 16 crores exceptional wage code charge. Management guided to 100 bps operating EBITDA margin expansion by exit FY27 and double-digit revenue growth, with early-to-mid teens cited.

segments.name: BPM
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 551 crores (+1.1% QoQ, +2.6% YoY); FY26 INR 2,170 crores, about 70% of revenue. EBITDA margin 16.3%, up 187 bps YoY.

segments.name: Tech and Digital
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 249 crores (+27.2% YoY); FY26 INR 910 crores, 29.6% of revenue (up 280 bps from 26.8%). EBITDA margin 12.1%, up 289 bps YoY.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 304 crores (+16.4% YoY), 38.1% of mix; FY26 mix 37.3%, up 180 bps. Healthcare (US) revenue crossed about USD 25 million in FY26.

guidance_outlook: Double-digit revenue growth in FY27-28; management quantified as early to mid-teens.
100 bps operating EBITDA margin expansion by exit of FY27 (Q4 FY27); mix (Tech and Digital and international) expected to contribute about 40% each, with operational efficiencies the rest.
FY31 target of INR 8,400 crores (USD 1 billion), of which about INR 1,700 crores inorganic; implies about 14-15% organic CAGR.
Healthcare expected at 12-15% of revenue by FY31 (USD 120-150 million); Tech and Digital at 40% and international at 50% of revenue by FY31.

Cash conversion baseline of about 70% of EBITDA; steady-state lease depreciation about INR 38-40 crores and PPE depreciation about INR 20 crores per year; management said at least one acquisition likely this year, with six targets evaluated and two at advanced stage.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR 105 crores, mainly technology platforms, AI capabilities and IT and leasehold infrastructure.

Annual cash deployment roughly INR 100 crores: maintenance capex INR 70-80 crores, plus INR 15-20 crores for two large leasehold premises moving in FY26-27; balance accrues for internal growth and inorganic deals.
AI centres of excellence set up in Bengaluru and Coimbatore for a global P&C insurance client, with the deal running on Azure.
Management stated no plans to monetise physical assets; premises are largely leased, with one owned premises.
demand_pricing: Q4 TCV INR 620 crores, second consecutive quarter above INR 600 crores; FY26 TCV INR 2,355 crores.
About 15% of pipeline is hyperscaler-led (AWS, GCP, Microsoft); management linked part of the 27% Tech and Digital growth to hyperscaler deal conversion.
Top-10 customer revenue concentration fell about 200 bps; of FY26 incremental revenue of about INR 205 crores, about 45% came from new customers.
Healthcare: two new US provider-side deals won in Q1 FY27 (per management); positioned as revenue cycle management, revenue enablement and CX partner; compared with Sagility as not like-for-like.
Revenue per FTE up 11.4% YoY to INR 584k, supported by AI-led delivery and pyramid optimisation.

qa_highlights.question: What was FY26 growth in USD terms, and how much came from existing versus new clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Constant-currency growth was 5.2%. About INR 205 crores of incremental revenue was added, with roughly 45% from new customers and the rest from existing clients.

qa_highlights.question: Is the standalone Digitide business loss-making once Alldigi profits are excluded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no; corporate costs sit in Digitide, including US and Canada sales leadership, and cost transfer pricing is applied, so standalone-versus-consolidated comparison is not like-for-like.

qa_highlights.question: What is sustainable OCF conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 70% of EBITDA is the baseline; FY26's 77% was boosted by novation catch-up after the demerger, with Q1 FY26 at -36%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the pipeline is hyperscaler-led and is it converting?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% of the pipeline is hyperscaler-led and contributions are now flowing through partners, with the Azure-based AI CoE deal cited.

qa_highlights.question: Will PulseNerve become a recurring platform or IP revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: PulseNerve is an orchestration layer enabling large AI service deals rather than a standalone platform; DocuSense, SmartPay and DigiCollect were cited as IP assets with non-linear revenue potential.

qa_highlights.question: What is the depreciation run-rate and what does EBIT look like after the Q4 changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one-time PPE depreciation charge is about INR 4 crores; steady-state lease depreciation is about INR 38-40 crores, with total depreciation around INR 60-62 crores, and the 100 bps margin guidance was reiterated. Net margin guidance was declined, with management pointing to an FY26 adjusted PAT margin of 2.3% as baseline.

risks_watch: Adjusted PAT fell to INR 11 crores in Q4 from INR 24 crores in Q3; management attributes this to lease and depreciation accounting, but the step-up in depreciation (Q4 INR 66 crores vs INR 49 crores a year earlier) and finance cost weigh on earnings.
Q4 EBITDA margin was flat at 11%, and management has pushed margin expansion timeline out; 100 bps expansion is now targeted by exit of FY27.
FY31 USD 1 billion target needs about 14-15% organic CAGR plus about INR 1,700 crores inorganic; inorganic progress and acquisition timing remain open.
Management declined to give a steady-state net profit margin, so analysts must derive it; reported PAT was INR (-5) crores in Q4 and INR 6 crores for FY26.
Watch whether DSO stays near 75 days and OCF conversion holds near 70% of EBITDA; watch hyperscaler pipeline conversion and healthcare wins.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and the FY27 outlook, but defensive and evasive on profitability: management repeatedly deflected questions on net margin, standalone profitability and EBIT, and framed Q4 weakness as accounting-driven.
key_quotes: What these numbers demonstrate is the absorptive capacity of our operational model.
We are looking at a strong 100-basis point expansion by the time we exit FY27.
Our normal target baseline for this is 70% conversion.
So, the 14% to 15% CAGR growth over the period is, we are very, very confident of that.
